<thought>
The 1H NMR shows:
- 1.20 ppm (d, J=7.1 Hz, 3H): methyl group coupled to CH
- 2.85 ppm (d, J=6.9 Hz, 2H): CH2 coupled to CH
- 3.09 ppm (qdd, J=7.1, 6.9, 6.9 Hz, 1H): CH coupled to both CH3 and CH2
- 3.81 ppm (s, 3H): methoxy group (OCH3)
- 7.15 ppm (ddd, J=8.5 Hz, 2H): aromatic protons (ortho to electron-donating group)
- 7.92 ppm (ddd, J=8.5 Hz, 2H): aromatic protons (ortho to electron-withdrawing group)

This suggests a para-disubstituted benzene ring with a methoxy group and another substituent. The pattern at 2.85 and 3.09 ppm suggests an isobutyl or similar branched alkyl chain.

Let me get the 13C NMR to confirm.

- A para-disubstituted benzene ring
- An ester group (C=O at 166.40 ppm, OCH3 at 52.24 ppm)
- An isobutyl group (CH3-CH-CH2-)

The structure appears to be: 4-isobutylbenzoic acid methyl ester (methyl 4-isobutylbenzoate)
